resources.string: Add a proxy to get started
You\'ll need the server address, port and type (HTTP or SOCKS5) from your proxy provider — plus a username and password if it uses one.
Apps use your normal network unless Android\'s system kill switch is on
Connecting isn\'t available in this build. It saves your proxies but doesn\'t connect.
Your phone\'s network is unchanged until the VPN starts. If the proxy check fails, nothing is switched over.
Android started ProxyFlow as your Always-on VPN: apps\' traffic is held until ProxyFlow reaches your proxy, never sent around it.
Approximate: what apps sent and received through your proxy since you connected.
Apps\' TCP connections go through your proxy
HTTPS sites stay encrypted end to end: ProxyFlow never decrypts them. TLS to proxy only encrypts the connection between this phone and your proxy.

resources.string: ProxyFlow carries TCP only: UDP is refused at once and pings get no reply, so calls, games and QUIC fall back to TCP or fail.
Apps\' traffic is paused until the proxy answers. ProxyFlow sends nothing around it.
Traffic paused — ProxyFlow sends nothing around your proxy
ProxyFlow is trying your proxy again. Apps stay paused until it answers.
Your phone has a network again. ProxyFlow is reconnecting to your proxy.
Your phone moved to another network. ProxyFlow is reconnecting to your proxy.
ProxyFlow will connect when a network is available. Traffic stays blocked meanwhile.
You\'re not connected: apps use your normal network unless Android\'s system kill switch is on.
Apps can\'t go online until this is fixed — ProxyFlow sends nothing around your proxy.
Apps will use your normal network, not your proxy, until you connect again.
Another VPN app was turned on, or ProxyFlow\'s VPN permission was removed.
Your apps no longer go through your proxy.
Android will ask you to allow ProxyFlow to set up a VPN. That is how apps\' connections reach your proxy on this phone.
ProxyFlow has no servers of its own and doesn\'t collect your traffic.
A key icon appears in the status bar while connected.
Only one VPN app can be active. Starting another turns ProxyFlow off.
ProxyFlow can\'t send your apps\' traffic to your proxy without Android\'s VPN permission. Nothing was changed on your phone.
The packet engine stopped while connected. Traffic stays blocked until you restart it or disconnect.
The profile this connection used was deleted, so its proxy isn\'t used any more. Traffic stays blocked until you stop the connection.
Android\'s system kill switch was on when last checked: if it still is, apps have no internet
Android said at %1$s that its system kill switch is off: while it is, apps use your normal network if ProxyFlow stops while connected.
Android said at %1$s that Always-on VPN is on without blocking: while it is, apps use your normal network if ProxyFlow stops while connected, until it connects again.
If ProxyFlow stops while connected, only Android\'s system kill switch keeps apps off your normal network.
Android said at %1$s that its system kill switch is on: while it is, apps have no internet when ProxyFlow isn\'t connected. To use your normal network, turn it off in Android\'s VPN settings.
Turn on Always-on VPN with \u201cBlock connections without VPN\u201d so Android blocks traffic when ProxyFlow isn\'t running.
Apps have no internet if \u201cBlock connections without VPN\u201d is on in Android\'s VPN settings; otherwise they use your normal network.
You\'re not connected. Android\'s system kill switch was on when ProxyFlow last checked: if it still is, apps have no internet.
Android\'s system kill switch was on when ProxyFlow last checked: if it still is, apps will have no internet until you connect again.
%1$s some time after it connected at %2$s.
Android removed the VPN with it: from then on apps used your normal network, unless Android\'s system kill switch was on.
After a restart ProxyFlow connects by itself only as your Always-on VPN: until then, apps use your normal network unless Android\'s system kill switch is on.
Android\'s system kill switch was on when ProxyFlow last checked before that: if it still was, apps had no internet until ProxyFlow connected again.
Android closed ProxyFlow to free memory
ProxyFlow stopped because of an error
ProxyFlow\'s packet engine stopped because of an error
Android closed ProxyFlow because it stopped responding
Android closed ProxyFlow after one of its permissions changed
If Android didn\'t ask, another app may be set as Always-on VPN: turn that off in VPN settings, then try again.
Your proxy stopped answering connection requests to several sites. ProxyFlow is reconnecting; apps stay paused until it answers.
Android started ProxyFlow as your Always-on VPN. Apps stay paused until ProxyFlow reaches your proxy.
Choose a proxy for Always-on VPN
Android started ProxyFlow as your Always-on VPN, but no proxy was chosen, so ProxyFlow didn\'t connect. Connect once with the proxy Always-on VPN should use.

ProxyFlow is using a proxy now. Choosing another one reconnects through it: open connections end, and apps can\'t go online until it\'s connected. If it can\'t connect, apps stay offline until you try again or stop. Nothing is sent around a proxy meanwhile.
ProxyFlow is still checking a proxy. Choosing another one checks that one instead, and apps use your normal network until it\'s connected.
